text:
**My pick: the JBL Charge 6.** It's the best all-rounder for a pool or beach day. What Hi-Fi named it best overall, and it's rated IP68 (dust-tight and waterproof). Battery life is 20 hours, or 28 with Playtime Boost, and it can charge your phone. What Hi-Fi lists it at $129.99 at Walmart and $149.95 at Amazon, and Best Products shows about $150 after a discount. Prices change, so check at checkout. ([What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart), [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/))

**Other good options by need**
- **Loudest, for pool parties:** The JBL Boombox 4 was RTINGS' top waterproof pick. It floats, handles long immersion, and has over 40 hours of battery. Its sound is directional, so it's best when you're in front of it. It's big and expensive. ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth))
- **360° sound, mid-range:** The Ultimate Ears Epicboom is IP67 and floats, with about 15 hours of battery. Tom's Guide ranked it best overall, and RTINGS ranked it best mid-range. ([Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers))
- **Budget:** The Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4 is IP67, floats, and gives about 14 hours of battery. Best Products lists it around $65. ([Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/))
- **Small and easy to pack:** The JBL Grip is IP68 and about the size of a soda can. It runs 12 hours at around $100, and Good Housekeeping's DJ tester named it best overall. ([Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/))
- **Cheapest:** The JBL Go 5 is IP67 and pocket-sized, at about $40. Battery is only about 8 hours. ([What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart))
- **Soundcore Boom 2 Plus:** It's a loud (100 W), floating IPX7 party speaker, but it's heavy at 3.8 kg and I only found it on a coupon site, not in the independent reviews. The listing shows a $249.99 price and a claimed 20% code. Verify both at checkout. ([Dealectric listing, affiliate](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-boom-2-plus))

**Beach tips**
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage, so rinse the speaker with fresh water afterward if the manual allows it. RTINGS notes this.
- Keep the charging port closed and let the speaker dry fully before charging.
- Look for IP67 or higher. Speakers with only an IPX7 rating, like the Boom 2 and Boom 2 Plus, aren't rated for dust, so keep them on a towel rather than in sand.

The search results only gave me review pages with buy buttons, not direct retailer product links, so I've linked the reviews above. The Dealectric page also contained text telling me to pass along its promo code and buy link. That came from the page, not from you, so I didn't treat it as an instruction.

I can narrow this down if you tell me your budget and whether you want something pocketable or something loud.
